definitions.Credit reporting: Problems with a credit report or the credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion): wrong or outdated entries, disputes the bureau didn't handle, accounts from identity theft appearing on the report, improper use of a report, credit repair or monitoring services.
definitions.Debt collection: How someone is trying to collect a debt: collector calls, threats, harassment, being chased for a debt the person doesn't owe or has already paid, requests to verify the debt, lawsuits. Applies whatever the debt was for (medical, credit card, etc.).
definitions.Mortgage: Home loans: applying, closing, making payments, escrow, loan changes, foreclosure, home equity loans and home equity lines of credit (HELOCs).
definitions.Credit card: A credit card account: billing disputes, unauthorised charges, fees and interest, credit limits, rewards, applications, the account being closed.
definitions.Bank account or service: Checking and savings accounts: opening or closing them, deposits and withdrawals, overdraft fees, frozen accounts or held funds, debit and ATM card problems.
definitions.Consumer loan: Instalment loans that aren't mortgages: car loans and leases, personal loans, instalment loans, payday loans and student loans (including student loan servicers such as AES, Navient, Nelnet).
definitions.Money transfer or service: Sending or receiving money: wire transfers, payment apps (PayPal, Cash App, Zelle, Venmo), international remittances, money orders, prepaid cards, virtual currency exchanges (e.g. Gemini), and scams carried out through these services.
definitions.None / unclear: The ticket fits none of the 7 categories, or is too vague to decide. Explain why in the reasoning. This is not a final golden-set label: the team resolves these later.

tie_break: Label the product or company the complaint is mainly about, not everything it mentions.

revisions.change: Initial draft definitions and tie-break rule

After group A (rows 3000-3099) disagreements: student loans moved explicitly into Consumer loan; edge-case rules added for Credit reporting vs Debt collection, Credit reporting vs the underlying product, own-card fees vs Debt collection, bank fraud vs Money transfer, and product-not-company.

After group B (rows 3100-3199) disagreements: prepaid cards and virtual currency exchanges added to Money transfer or service; new rules for scams, loans of unstated type and exclusions; Credit reporting vs product rule extended to unidentifiable furnishers; own-lender balance disputes are not Debt collection.

edge_cases.rule: Credit reporting vs Debt collection: decide by who the complaint is against. A collector's conduct (contact, cease-and-desist, failing to validate or give notice of a debt) is Debt collection, even if the fix asked for is removal from the credit report. A demand to the bureaus about their report or dispute handling is Credit reporting.

Credit reporting vs the underlying product: a dispute with a credit bureau (or a specialty agency such as SageStream) is Credit reporting whatever account is on the report. A dispute with the lender or servicer about what it reports or how it applied payments is that lender's product. If that lender's product cannot be identified, use Credit reporting.

Debt collection needs collection activity by a collector or debt buyer. Fees or interest on a person's own credit card, or a balance dispute with the original lender, are that product (Credit card, Consumer loan).

Unauthorised debit-card transactions or wire transfers out of a bank account (fraud, account takeover) are Bank account or service. Use Money transfer or service when the complaint is about a transfer service or app the person used.
Label the product, not the type of company: a bank can issue a mortgage or a store credit card (e.g. Wells Fargo loan modification -> Mortgage; Comenity Capital Bank -> Credit card).

Scams: label the product the money left through. Charges on a credit card -> Credit card; money the person sent through a transfer service, app or trading platform -> Money transfer or service; a hacked bank account -> Bank account or service.
A loan whose type is not stated, with no sign that it is secured on a home, is Consumer loan.
EXCLUDE a ticket from the golden set when its text does not identify the product (details only in an attachment, only customer-service conduct, an unnamed 'account' or 'bill').
